correctness.rationale: The empty and singleton sets fail, and for two landmarks the first and last edges of a shortest path collide, with the adjacent-landmark case covered by minimum degree two. For the infinite construction use the three top-rail columns 0,j,N, with j=2 for even N>=6 and j=3 for odd N>=9. In the right region each signature has the distinguished j-spaced pair (q-j,q) and third entry N-q+c with c in {-1,0,1}; equal distinguished pairs identify the edge. A collision with different pairs forces c'=c-j and 2q=N+c-j, impossible for j=3 and impossible by parity for j=2. In the left region the listed triples are distinct and only the first rung has a j-spaced pair. Its pair (0,j) would force q=j on the right, where the third entry is strictly below N. Independent BFS and subset enumeration of the exceptional orders checks all subsets at n=2,3,4 and all sizes through four at n=5,6,8. It reproduces the infinite dimensions, absence of smaller bases at 5,6,8, and the 4,20,80 basis counts; it also found four three-sets at n=7. The referenced finite_obstructions.json is absent in the frozen package and was not validated; the independent enumeration establishes the required finite facts without it.
residual_risks: The finite replay is not the proof of the tail; that part was reviewed symbolically. The missing original certificate was not authenticated.

checked_sources: Ikhlaq et al., original invariant and comb-product comparison
value.rationale: The two-row Cartesian grid is a basic test family for an order-insensitive distance invariant. The result separates nonexistence from low finite dimension, supplies a uniform construction, and shows a genuine isolated reversal of the naïve monotonicity expectation at eight columns. Exact labelled basis multiplicities quantify that exceptional regime rather than merely producing isolated witnesses.
residual_risks: The finding does not classify optimal triples in general or imply a theorem on wider rectangular grids.
